name: cloudflared
description: Cloudflare Tunnel connector (remotely-managed tunnel 'fleet-edge') — the network half of the Cloudflare One (Zero Trust) edge. Outbound-only: no inbound port is opened anywhere. Hostnames, Access apps and ingress rules are declared in cloud-infra c_vps/ba-clo_cloudflare (terraform.json .zero_trust + zero-trust.tf); this container only carries the connector. Origins are reached over the WireGuard mesh (10.0.0.0/24), so one tunnel can front any VM. Design: cloud-infra a0_docs/eng-specs/cloudflare-zero-trust.md. Caddy + Authelia on gcp-proxy stay the fallback path and do not depend on this.

app._doc_image: Pinned (released 2026-09-24), multi-arch (arm64 for oci-apps). The image ENTRYPOINT is `cloudflared --no-autoupdate`; bumps are deliberate, never a silent :latest pull.
app._doc_command: Remotely-managed tunnel: `run` with no name reads TUNNEL_TOKEN from the env (sops secret). Ingress lives in Cloudflare (terraform), not in a local config.yml. Metrics + /ready on 127.0.0.1:20241 only (host network, loopback bind).
app._doc_network_mode: host: origins are WG-mesh addresses (10.0.0.x) and the connector must reach them exactly as the host does. Nothing listens publicly — the only socket is the loopback metrics bind.

monitoring._doc: No vhost of its own. Health = the tunnel's connector status in Cloudflare (cf-zero-trust workflow [zt:probe]) and http://127.0.0.1:20241/ready on oci-apps.

secrets._doc: TUNNEL_TOKEN — the remotely-managed tunnel token (base64 of account id + tunnel id + tunnel secret). Produced by terraform (output zt_tunnel_token) and written by the cf-zero-trust pilot runner straight into a sops file encrypted to the public age recipient; copied here verbatim as src/secrets.tunnel.yaml (a secret FRAGMENT). Never stored in plaintext anywhere.
